LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard build process for the `bde-verify` tool, a static analysis utility for BDE C++ standards. It fetches source code from the official GitHub repository (`https://github.com/bloomberg/bde_verify.git`) using Git, which is an expected and legitimate source. The `sha256sums=(SKIP)` is appropriate here because the source is a Git repository (a VCS source), and checksums are not applicable — this is a common and accepted practice in AUR packages for `-git` packages.

The build process uses standard tools (CMake, Ninja) and compiles the code with Clang 21, as expected. It modifies `CMakeLists.txt` to adapt the build for Arch Linux's library layout (e.g., unified `clang-cpp` and LLVM libraries), which is normal packaging adaptation. The `package()` function installs files correctly, relocates libraries from `/usr/lib64` to `/usr/lib` (common on Arch), and handles configuration files with a symlink for compatibility — all standard and safe operations. There are no network operations during build, no use of `eval`, no obfuscated code, and no suspicious downloads or executions.

No evidence of malicious behavior, data exfiltration, or supply-chain attacks is present. All actions align with legitimate packaging practices for an AUR Git package.
</details>
